user-story.i-want: agentic orchestration framework integrated per Architect's selection
user-story.so-that: multi-step analytical workflows can be planned and executed

acceptance-criteria.criterion: AWS Strands framework (v1.15.0) installed and configured in RAGLite - Package added to pyproject.toml dependencies - Import verification test passes - Version pinned to v1.15.0+ (Apache 2.0 licensed)

Framework initialization and configuration validated - Strands Agent class instantiable with basic config - Mistral Small configured as orchestration LLM (tunable to Claude) - OpenTelemetry observability configured (optional, can defer to Story 3.5)

Basic 2-step workflow execution tested - Test workflow: Retrieval Agent → Synthesis Agent (simple pipeline) - Workflow accepts query input and returns structured output - State passes correctly between agents (query → retrieval results → synthesis)

State management functional for multi-step workflows - Agent execution state captured and propagated - Context passes between sequential agents - State validation confirms data integrity across agent boundaries

Error handling implemented for workflow failures (NFR24, NFR26) - Agent timeout handling (max 15s per agent, per NFR26) - Graceful degradation on agent failures (fallback to Epic 2 simple search) - Error logging with structured metadata (agent ID, failure reason, timestamp)

Integration test validates framework execution - End-to-end test with mock agents (no real LLM calls) - Test validates agent coordination and state flow - Test execution time <1s (framework overhead only, no LLM latency)

Documentation includes workflow development guide - Workflow pattern examples documented - Agent creation guide (how to add new agents) - Debugging guide (OpenTelemetry traces, logs) - Code examples for common patterns

constraints.constraint: KISS Principle: Keep It Simple, Stupid - No custom base classes, factories, or abstractions beyond what Strands provides
Target: 50 LOC for orchestration (per framework selection doc) - Stay within code budget
Event-driven pattern: Use Strands' agents-as-tools pattern, not imperative orchestration
NFR26: Agent timeout 15s max per agent. Total workflow <20s p95 to match Epic 2 baseline
Orchestration overhead budget: 3-5s (validated in POC during Story 3-0-8)
NFR24: Graceful degradation required - fallback to Epic 2 simple search on agentic workflow failures
Use mock agents for testing (no real LLM calls) - Real LLM integration in Stories 3.2-3.4
Framework overhead test must execute <1s (measures framework only, no LLM latency)
Tech stack is LOCKED - AWS Strands v1.15.0 already approved in Story 3-0-8, but any additional dependencies require user approval

tests.standards: Follow existing RAGLite testing patterns: Unit tests in tests/unit/agentic/, integration tests in tests/integration/. Use pytest with pytest-asyncio for async tests. Mock external dependencies (LLM calls) using pytest-mock. Target 80%+ coverage. Parallel execution with pytest-xdist where safe (no shared state). Test discovery validates all tests found by pytest.

dev-notes.note: This story implements the foundation for Epic 3's agentic orchestration based on Story 3-0-8 spike findings. Framework selected: AWS Strands v1.15.0. Architecture designed: 3-agent pipeline (Retrieval → Analysis → Synthesis). Fallback strategy: Simple Function Calling if AWS Strands has blockers on Day 1.

New module structure: raglite/agentic/ containing orchestrator.py, agents/ directory with mock agents for testing, and state.py for AgentState Pydantic model. Mock agents used in this story - real agent implementations in Stories 3.2-3.4.
Performance targets: Total query latency <10s p50, <20s p95. Orchestration overhead: 3-5s. Individual agent timeout: 15s max (NFR26). Framework overhead test must execute <1s without LLM calls.

Testing isolation: Use mock agents to avoid LLM API costs and latency. Real LLM integration tested in Stories 3.2-3.4 when implementing actual Retrieval, Analysis, and Synthesis agents. Focus on framework mechanics and state management in this story.

Graceful degradation (NFR24): If agentic workflow fails (timeout, agent error, framework issue), fallback to Epic 2 simple search (raglite.retrieval.multi_index_search). Log failure with structured metadata for debugging.
